name: Baseten

modes.label: H100 MIG 40GB, serverless (×1)
modes.note: Source: https://docs.baseten.co/deployment/resources ESTIMATOR EXCLUDED: Fractional slice cannot be represented by a full-GPU map. Exact researched rate remains in gpu.json.

modes.label: CPU-only instance (dedicated deployment)
modes.note: Per-minute list prices x60. Shared CPU instance types; cannot select a region. Truss model-serving containers, not general sandboxes.

plans.name: Basic
plans.note: $0 per month, pay as you go. Invoiced when usage exceeds $50 or at month end until payment history is established. If credits run out with no payment method, models are deactivated.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Unlimited autoscaling and priority compute access; priority access to high-demand GPUs; volume discounts; quote only.

caveats: Bundled CPU/RAM; billed by minute. Deployment/load/scale time billed; scale-to-zero is not free warm replicas. H100 MIG is 3/7 compute and 1/2 memory, not half a full H100. Custom model packaging via Truss; not a general secure code-exec sandbox.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Larger CPU/RAM shapes on the same GPU cost more (T4x8x32 $0.01504/min, T4x16x64 $0.02408/min, A10Gx16x64 $0.03248/min); multi-GPU SKUs are linear (H100:8 $0.86664/min). Card models only the smallest single-GPU shape.
Image builds are billed on every push; cold start/model load is billed; failed boots and image pulls are not; development deployments (--watch) are listed as not billed. Partial minutes round up.
Default autoscaling scale-down delay is 900 s (configurable 0-3600 s): with defaults each burst keeps the replica billed ~15 more idle minutes, plus billed cold start/model load. Not modelled.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.verification: payment method after credits; org verification for regional deployments
fleet.tiers: Pro advertises 'Unlimited autoscaling and priority compute access'; per-deployment max_replica defaults to 1 (user-adjustable); organization-level concurrent GPU limits exist (docs example: 16 H100) and are raised by contacting Baseten
fleet.notes: Default org GPU quota for a new Basic workspace is not published.

snapshot_auto.quote: cold start = container pull + weight load + engine initialization
snapshot_auto.note: Scale-to-zero shuts replicas down; on wake a fresh replica is started (image pull, weight load, engine init). No state checkpoint/restore of replicas is documented. Speed-ups come from caches (BDN weight cache, b10cache torch.compile cache), not machine snapshots.

harness_api.quote: Use [Baseten Switch](/reference/cli/baseten-switch) to route requests from Claude Code or Codex CLI to Model APIs.
harness_api.note: Baseten is a model-serving/training platform, not an agent sandbox. Its coding-agent features are an LLM routing CLI (Baseten Switch) and an MCP/skill to manage the workspace; nothing runs or drives an agent harness inside a Baseten container.

egress_allowlist.quote: On request, model replicas and supporting services can run without direct internet access, with outbound traffic limited to an approved allow-list.
egress_allowlist.note: Enterprise single-tenant only, configured by Baseten on request (not self-serve); allow-list granularity (domain vs IP) not stated. Self-hosted: customer's own VPC network policies. Standard Baseten Cloud: no egress control documented.

ingress_rules.quote: You can also restrict inference to a specific IP range or to traffic originating within your VPC.
ingress_rules.note: All Baseten Cloud endpoints are API-key authenticated (environment-scoped / model-scoped inference-only keys available); single-tenant adds PrivateLink / Private Service Connect and IP-range restriction. SSH to replicas uses short-lived certs limited to users who can manage the model.

guest_firewall.quote: Your container runs as the non-root `app` user.
guest_firewall.note: Kubernetes containers (Calico/Cilium network isolation); 'Workloads and nodes run with minimal privileges'. No root or NET_ADMIN, so iptables/nftables inside is not possible.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are passed as keyword arguments to the `Model` class.
secret_proxy.note: Workspace/team secret store (UI + Management API); secrets are delivered into the container (kwargs / env for custom servers, training SecretReference). Also OIDC short-lived tokens and AWS AssumeRole for cloud access. No injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Mount existing BDN volumes into your model container at runtime.
volume_attach.note: BDN volumes: versioned, immutable file trees, mounted read-only ('The mount is read-only.'); `baseten volume` CLI is PRE-RELEASE. Also b10cache (network volume at /cache/org and /cache/model, read-write, 'treat it as a cache') and the training cache ($BT_PROJECT_CACHE_DIR / $BT_TEAM_CACHE_DIR). No generic block volumes.

volume_shared.quote: It's a volume mounted over the network onto each of your replicas, with two scopes:
volume_shared.note: b10cache is read-write and shared: /cache/org/ 'Shared across every replica you deploy in your organization', /cache/model/ per deployment; not durable storage. BDN volumes are shared read-only across deployments; training cache is shared by all jobs in a project/team on one cluster.

isolation.quote: You're connected when you see a shell prompt inside the model container.
isolation.note: Kubernetes-orchestrated containers, not full VMs; card already models isolation=container.

image_oci.quote: Set `base_image` to your image and use `docker_server` to specify how to start it
image_oci.note: Custom Docker/OCI base images supported via docker_server/base_image config.

docker_inside.quote: Your container runs as the non-root `app` user.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Model containers are single-purpose serving containers with no root/privileged access; running Docker-in-Docker is not documented.

nested_virt.quote: Your container runs as the non-root `app` user.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No /dev/kvm or nested virtualization documented for a non-root Kubernetes pod.

desktop.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Baseten is a model-serving/inference platform, not a desktop/VNC provider.

browser.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed browser product is documented.

computer_use.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot/click desktop-driving API is documented.

anti_bot.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Baseten serves models, not stealth/anti-bot browsing infrastructure.

captcha_solving.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature documented; not relevant to a model-serving GPU cloud.

egress_ip_type.quote: Restricted egress: On request, model replicas and supporting services can run without direct internet access, with outbound traffic limited to an approved allow-list.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard cloud egress runs from Baseten's/cloud-provider's datacenter IP ranges; no residential/mobile egress product exists.

ssh.quote: SSH into any running model deployment on Baseten and get a full terminal inside the model container
ssh.note: Requires org to enable Inference SSH and enabling it per deployment in config.yaml.

snapshot.quote: cold start = container pull + weight load + engine initialization
snapshot.note: Scale-to-zero starts a fresh replica from the image on wake; no filesystem or memory snapshot/restore of a replica is documented. Caches (BDN weight cache, b10cache) speed cold starts but are not full machine snapshots.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: cold start = container pull + weight load + engine initialization
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI to take an on-demand snapshot/checkpoint of a running deployment is documented.

fork.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Baseten scales by adding fresh replicas from the same image, not by cloning a running machine's state.

fork_running.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No clone-a-running-machine capability documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: cold start = container pull + weight load + engine initialization
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-inclusive clone/fork feature exists; new replicas always cold-start from the image.

pause_resume.quote: Choose 'Enabled' switch to pause it without removing it.
pause_resume.note: The 'Enabled' toggle removes/disables a deployment (scales to zero replicas) rather than pausing a live machine with reduced billing state preserved; pause/resume documented elsewhere refers to rolling-deployment traffic promotion, not machine pause. No true machine-level pause/resume with preserved state is documented.

persistent_disk.quote: It's a volume mounted over the network onto each of your replicas
persistent_disk.note: Container filesystem itself is ephemeral per replica; durable storage is via BDN volumes (versioned/read-only) or b10cache (explicitly a cache, not durable), not a generic persistent root disk that survives stop/start of a given machine.

live_resize.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Changing instance type/resources requires a redeploy, not a live in-place resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: Use Baseten Switch to route requests from Claude Code or Codex CLI to Model APIs.
agent_harnesses.note: Baseten Switch is a local gateway that routes an already-installed coding agent's requests to Baseten Model APIs; no coding agent runs preinstalled inside a Baseten sandbox/container.

own_agent_api.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Baseten is a model-inference/training platform; it has no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent product.

mcp_server.quote: Add the backend MCP server at https://api.baseten.co/mcp with the header "Authorization: Bearer $BASETEN_MCP_KEY". Add the docs MCP server at https://docs.baseten.co/mcp.
mcp_server.note: Baseten ships an MCP server (plus a docs MCP server) so an agent can manage the Baseten workspace/sandboxes.

lang_python.quote: Baseten installs your Python dependencies, packages the `Model` class into a container, and deploys it.
lang_python.note: Python is the primary first-party runtime (Truss Model class, Python SDK).

lang_node.quote: To switch to Baseten with the JavaScript SDK, change `baseURL` and `apiKey` when initializing the client
lang_node.note: Node/JavaScript is only offered as a client SDK for calling deployed models over HTTP; there is no first-party Node.js runtime for packaging/running your own model code inside a Baseten container (that path is Python/Truss, or bring-your-own Docker image).

public_ipv4.quote: Private networking: You control inference ingress through your load balancer, security groups, and provider-native networking controls.
public_ipv4.note: Inference is reached via Baseten-issued HTTPS API endpoints; no documented dedicated/public IPv4 address per model deployment.

egress_http_rules.quote: Restricted egress: On request, model replicas and supporting services can run without direct internet access, with outbound traffic limited to an approved allow-list.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control exists only as a coarse allow-list (enterprise single-tenant, on request), not documented at HTTP method/path granularity.

static_egress_ip.quote: Restricted egress: On request, model replicas and supporting services can run without direct internet access, with outbound traffic limited to an approved allow-list.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP address is documented; egress allow-listing is domain/destination based, not a guaranteed static source IP.

windows.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All model deployment compute is Linux containers; Windows only appears as a client OS for the CLI/SSH tooling.

macos.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No macOS compute product; macOS only appears as a client OS (CLI, Baseten Switch) for developers.

arm64.quote: Baseten is a platform for deploying and serving AI models.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Baseten's deployment compute (GPU and CPU-only instances) is x86_64; ARM only appears for client-side CLI binaries (macOS arm64 laptops), not server-side compute.

open_source.quote: The `config.yaml` follows Truss, Baseten's open-source model packaging format.
open_source.note: Truss (model packaging format/CLI) is open source, but the core Baseten serving platform/control plane itself is closed-source SaaS.

sso.quote: Baseten supports any SAML 2.0 IdP and any SCIM 2.0 directory provider through WorkOS, including: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Google Workspace.
sso.note: SSO and SCIM available on the Enterprise plan.

max_session_h.note: No documented maximum runtime for a deployment/replica; deployments run continuously (subject to autoscaling/scale-to-zero) until removed, billed per minute like an always-on VM.

cpu_class.quote: Deployments on shared CPU instance types can't select a region. ... Models run on a multi-tenant infrastructure layer with namespace- and container-level isolation, and GPUs are never shared across customers.
cpu_class.note: Docs explicitly call the non-GPU tier 'shared CPU instance types' (high confidence for cpu-only). For GPU-attached tiers, Baseten Cloud is described as multi-tenant with namespace/container isolation and states only that 'GPUs are never shared across customers' -- it does not extend that dedicated guarantee to vCPUs, and all instances (GPU and CPU-only) are Kubernetes containers on shared nodes (isolation=container). Applying the same shared-vCPU characterization to GPU tiers is a reasonable inference (medium confidence) rather than a directly-quoted per-tier statement.

usage_api.quote: Baseten bills each running replica by the minute. Billing and usage information is available through the Management API and the dashboard, but per-replica or per-deployment cost breakdown is not exposed via API.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; Baseten's API provides organization-level billing and usage data (account-only granularity) with cost information, but does not support per-sandbox/per-deployment usage queries or per-tag/per-project filtering needed for multi-tenant customer billing allocation.
